output.summary: The PR changes the bounds check in src/bounds.ts from `index < length` to `index <= length`, causing index == length to be accepted as in-bounds. This violates the documented contract that valid integer indices for a collection of length N are 0 through N-1, and it breaks the empty-collection case (length 0 has no valid index).

findings.title: Off-by-one regression: index equal to length is incorrectly reported as in-bounds
findings.body: Changing `index < length` to `index <= length` makes `inBounds(index, length)` return true when index == length. Per the contract, valid indices for a nonnegative integer length N are 0 through N-1, so index == length must return false. For length 0 (empty collection), every index, including 0, must be out of bounds, but the new expression returns true for index 0. The frozen counterexamples confirm this: {index:3,length:3} expected false but observed true, and {index:0,length:0} expected false but observed true. This can lead to out-of-bounds access by any caller relying on this helper.
findings.evidence: src/bounds.ts line 2 reads `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. Synthetic CI counterexamples report {index:3,length:3} expected false/observed true and {index:0,length:0} expected false/observed true.
findings.suggestion: Restore the original comparison: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`.

output.diagnosis: The diff replaced the strict upper-bound comparison `<` with `<=`, allowing the out-of-range boundary value index == length to pass, contradicting the stated contract and the test expectations.
